region: North Texas reservoir shore (Lake Ray Hubbard): blackland prairie clays, bermuda lawns, post oak and cedar elm woods, limestone shingle, drought-exposed bed
_about: Track A ground card (shore plan, Nov 16 2026): the eight ground surfaces of Lake Ray Hubbard's shore, their CC0 sources, real sizes and target colours. One region pack (Tools/envloop/ground/pack.py) is the source of truth for the ground material (ground_material.py, ground_hlsl.py), the prep script and Track B's blade tips (albedo_linear is linear RGB, the mean the material draws, before wetness). Sizes are the source scan's real width; px_per_m is what each tier keeps (hero band rule: 1 cm per pixel or finer).

surfaces.name: Mown bermuda lawn
surfaces.where: Mown yards and the club lawn (the Mown mask from the house and club footprints), on gentle slopes above 0.8 m over the pool
surfaces.feature_note: bermuda blade width 1.5-3 mm, mown height 40-60 mm (plan size table); the scan shows blade clusters 3-6 mm wide
surfaces.albedo_note: Summer: irrigated bermuda, sRGB about (94, 106, 68) (round 1's (92, 109, 61) read too saturated after the tone curve). Dormant (Dec-Mar in north Texas): straw tan, sRGB about (148, 133, 102). Provisional until Bean's grey-card ground photos.

surfaces.name: Rough dry grass
surfaces.where: Unmown fields, low flats back from the water, road verges and steep grassy banks: anywhere grass that is not in the Mown mask
surfaces.feature_note: size not published; set from its grass tufts (2-3 cm across) and dead stems
surfaces.albedo_note: Summer: little bluestem and johnsongrass with brown thatch, sRGB about (108, 110, 77). Dormant: straw, sRGB about (141, 133, 104).

surfaces.name: Blackland clay
surfaces.where: Steep and eroded faces, bare banks above the swash, cut banks: the slope term
surfaces.feature_note: crumbly clods 1-4 cm, the dry crumb of a Houston Black / Austin series vertisol
surfaces.albedo_note: Dry blackland clay is a dark grey brown, sRGB about (108, 99, 87); the tan wave-cut faces of the lake's banks are a little lighter (the vertex colour's bank tone carries that).

surfaces.name: Limestone gravel
surfaces.where: Wave-washed shingle on exposed points (0.1 to 0.7 m over the water, on the shore cells), the club's paths and lots (Track H later)
surfaces.feature_note: crushed limestone 3/4 inch and under (8-25 mm stones)
surfaces.albedo_note: Weathered, dirty crushed limestone at the waterline (silt film, algae stain), sRGB about (141, 137, 128); clean white crushed stone (0.33+) read as a painted patch in round 1.

surfaces.name: Sand
surfaces.where: The club beach and the lighter bank cells (the vertex colour's sandy bank tone), swash zone 0 to 0.5 m
surfaces.feature_note: trampled sand-clay: crust, ripples and footprints 1-4 cm; single grains (0.1-2 mm) are below a pixel at every tier, as they are to the eye at 3 m
surfaces.albedo_note: Tan reservoir beach sand (brought-in concrete sand over clay), sRGB about (149, 137, 117).

surfaces.name: Wet mud
surfaces.where: The swash band (the water's edge to about 0.3 m over it) and the bed just under the surface
surfaces.albedo_note: Saturated clay mud, already wet: dark olive brown, sRGB about (82, 76, 64). Its wetness is in the albedo, so the wet term only lowers its roughness.

surfaces.name: Cracked dry mud
surfaces.where: Lake bed left dry when the lake is under its pool (the gauge level): below 0 m pool height, above the water by 0.15 m or more, gentle slopes
surfaces.albedo_note: Dried lake silt crust, grey tan, sRGB about (117, 110, 97); 0.205 read as concrete at 15 m in round 1.

surfaces.name: Leaf litter
surfaces.where: Under trees (the vertex colour's canopy tone) and in the wooded banks
surfaces.feature_note: post oak and cedar elm leaves 3-12 cm, twigs, patches of moss
surfaces.albedo_note: Oak litter under shade, brown with green moss, sRGB about (93, 87, 66); winter adds fresh fallen leaves, warmer.
